judgments.reasoning_cat1: The escape hatch turns on the Company deciding 'the services are substantially complete', a vague standard with no defined measure and no named services, and the sentence also fixes the 'Retention Period' as a defined term while simultaneously letting it end early.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its promise of 'full payment ... without proration' on early completion sits against Section 2.a, which prorates the Payment when employment ends by Company-initiated severance or transfer, and against Section 10's at-will/no-employment-rights language, so it is unclear which regime governs an early Company-driven end.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The amount, trigger and 15-business-day window are definite, and the clause expressly subordinates itself to adjustment, forfeiture and timing provisions, leaving little to construe on its own words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It depends entirely on Sections 2.a-2.d, 12 and 14 for its actual operation; those cross-references are broadly consistent, though the competing 'notwithstanding' overrides in 2.c and 14 make the payment obligation less than fully harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is badly corrupted mid-sentence ('sniclilig bes ony payment') so the scope of the employee's tax responsibility is not readable, and 'IBAS' is an undefined acronym whose terms are incorporated wholesale.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the Agreement defines IBAS or addresses hypothetical tax, so the incorporation dangles, but no other provision contradicts the withholding right.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Payment may be affected by a change in your duties or position as set forth below' is permissive and open-ended, and 'affected' is not tied to any particular mechanism in the fragment itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It points forward to Section 2.a, which prorates only on a transfer 'out of the position you held at the start of the Retention Period' — narrower than 'a change in your duties', so a duties change short of a transfer has an unallocated effect; it also overlaps Section 4's at-will language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Company initiated severance' is an undefined phrase carrying more than one reasonable reading (any Company-initiated termination, or only a formal severance-program separation), and 'transferred out of the position you held' is equally uncertain as against a mere change of duties or reorganisation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Section 4, which lets the Company terminate 'with or without cause' at any time, and Section 2.b, which forfeits on resignation or retirement, a for-cause dismissal falls into no category at all; it also conflicts with the Term clause's 'full payment ... without proration' on early completion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Resignation or retirement (other than retirement in connection with a Company initiated severance)' rests on the same undefined 'Company initiated severance' and gives no guidance on constructive discharge or a resignation solicited by the Company.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the mirror image of Section 2.a and must be read against Section 4's unrestricted termination right; together they leave a for-cause or mutual separation unassigned to either the forfeiture or the proration track.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any 1 amount of the Payment' is a mechanical corruption that obscures whether all or only the unpaid portion is forfeited, and the enumerated triggers include the wholly subjective '(i) you failed to meet performance expectations' and the boundless '(vi) violated the Company Code of Conduct in any respect', with (v) functioning as an open-ended catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'Notwithstanding any provision hereof to the contrary' opener directly overrides the proration promise in Section 2.a and the payment obligation in Section 1, and it competes with the separate 'notwithstanding' forfeiture in Section 14 and with Section 12's bar on diminishing accrued rights.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In the case of certain leaves of absences' identifies no class of leaves at all, and the proviso's 'may be paid to you earlier' leaves the accelerated payment wholly discretionary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Deeming employment to continue 'unchanged' during leave sits awkwardly beside Section 2.c's performance-based forfeiture and Section 2.a's transfer trigger, but no other provision squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prohibition is a standard anti-alienation formula; 'until the Agreement has expired' is the only loose edge, since the Agreement can end by termination rather than expiry.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with Section 2.a's payment to 'your estate' on death and with Section 8's successor clause; nothing in the instrument permits an assignment it forbids.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The language is a conventional at-will disclaimer with clear terms; 'with or without cause and with or without notice' is definite rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its unrestricted termination right must be squared with Sections 2.a and 2.b, which make the Payment turn on the character of the separation, and with the fixed two-year Retention Period in the Term clause — a for-cause dismissal fits none of the payment categories.
